ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS polyline runs 10.78 km between the recorded pickup event (08:35:15) and the recorded dropoff event (09:03:15), against a platform optimal of 7.2 km — an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of the optimal — which clears both POL-RD-01 gates: more than 20% of the optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field where the two distance figures disagree, and the trace figure (10.78 km) is the one the threshold test is run on; the trip record's rounded 10.8 km is a convenience copy and may not be cited for the test. On either reading the excess is well over the 1.44 km (20% of 7.2 km) trigger.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 169 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and requires no corroboration from an independent source.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on the face of the bundle: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-00106, and the pickup sequence is consistent across them (requested 08:29:50, driver arrived 08:33:40, trip started 08:35:15).

POL-RD-08's heightened-corroboration condition does not fire against this rider: deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 1, so no evidence beyond the gps_trace is required to sustain the claim. I cite the rider profile only for the test POL-RD-08 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires; no other field on that profile is used as a ground of decision.

On the POL-RD-02 recomputation the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary: charged_total 26.04; recomputed_fare 15.32, being ((3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00106, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP lying on the optimal route); refund 10.72; amount payable rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.75. That is 41.2% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND and not the 90% full-refund route.

The $5.50 of ERP the rider objects to is comprehended inside that refund and must not be added on top of it. The optimal route carries no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00, and the routing engine's own optimal description names no gantry), so a recomputed fare built on the optimal route excludes both charged gantries; POL-RD-09(1) is explicit that adding the off-route pass-through again would double-count. The correct figure is 10.75, not 16.25.

Both charged gantries are crossings of the vehicle on this trace, not phantom lines: the nearest fix to the CTE (Braddell Rd) gantry is 0.0 m at 08:40:55 and to the CTE (Chin Swee Rd tunnel) gantry 24.1 m at 08:52:45, each well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) prescribes. Both are flagged on_optimal_route false, so the gantry data independently places the vehicle on the CTE corridor that the platform's own booked optimal (Thomson Rd to Bukit Timah Rd to Rochor Canal Rd) does not traverse.

No traffic advisory can exonerate the detour under POL-RD-03. The only advisory artifact in the bundle is MISSING — I disclose the impairment: weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and it records that no LTA advisory covers Thomson Rd, the CTE or the Chin Swee tunnel in the 08:29-09:03 window on 17 July 2026. Absence is itself citable, and limb (c) of POL-RD-03's test cannot be met where no advisory names any affected road.

POL-RD-04 cannot excuse the route either. The chat log holds exactly one message, from the rider: 'why we at havelock? bugis is behind us', sent 08:46:30 and read but never answered. That is a complaint about the route in progress, not an instruction identifying a place or road to be driven to, and waypoint_hint is null — so the clause's 200 m corroboration test cannot be run on this record and no rider-requested detour is made out.

POL-RD-05 does not apply. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so no relocation of either endpoint occurred and no distance needs to be excluded from excess before the threshold test; the booked optimal of 7.2 km is the correct baseline.

POL-RD-12 does not apply. vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no matched pooled itinerary inflating the baseline and nothing turns on a co-rider's collection or set-down; the 7.2 km figure is the field the POL-RD-01 test runs on.

POL-RD-11 does not close the refund route. fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so no upfront quote fixed the distance and time charges at booking and the rider is not already whole on those lines; POL-RD-02 governs and the distance-and-time refund runs.

The burden has shifted to the driver under POL-RD-08 and has not been discharged. No counterparty_statement is on file, the rider's single in-app query about being at Havelock went unanswered, and no artifact and no clause is invoked on the driver's side of the record. A general assertion that the route was necessary is not evidence, and on this bundle the rider's case stands unrebutted.

The POL-RD-01 threshold test is run on the trace, and on the governing trace figure the excess is only 3.58 km — 49.72% of the 7.2 km optimal route. That sits below the 50% materiality line and far below the 8.0 km absolute line, so this is at most an ordinary established deviation and not a MATERIAL one. The trip_record's 10.8 km is a rounded convenience copy that POL-RD-01 expressly forbids citing for the threshold test; the trace's 10.78 km governs, and it is that figure which keeps the case under the materiality gate.

Even if the driver_profile is consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 96 completed trips in 90 days, a ratio of 0.000, under both the 3-flag test and the 0.05 ratio test (which needs at least 40 trips). With no pattern established, the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) arises. Only the two fields POL-RD-06 names may be used for this test.

Any remedy is the POL-RD-02 arithmetic and nothing beyond it: charged_total 26.04 less recomputed_fare 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to 10.75. The $5.50 of off-route ERP the rider complains of is already comprehended inside that figure under POL-RD-09(1), because the recomputed fare includes only gantries lying on the optimal route and the optimal route carries none — so the ERP must never be added on top. Both the rider's $26.04 demand and any 10.75 + 5.50 = 16.25 variant are overstated; the correct single figure is 10.75.

There is no billing-integrity defect to bolt onto the refund under POL-RD-09(4). Both charged gantries are genuinely crossed: the trace's nearest fixes sit 0.0 m and 24.1 m from the two gantry coordinates, well inside the 250 m match radius, so neither line is a phantom charge. No standalone pass-through correction is available, and the ERP figures must not be counted a second time.

The rider's demand for the full $26.04 cannot be reached. FULL_REFUND is available only through a MATERIAL deviation carrying an established POL-RD-06 pattern, or through a POL-RD-02 refund reaching 90% of charged_total. Here the deviation is non-material at 49.72% and the POL-RD-02 refund is only 41.2% of the charge, with reaches_full_refund_share false. The remedy is therefore capped at the partial refund of 10.75, and the driver should not be ordered to give up any more.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this trip is a genuine route deviation and part of the fare must be returned.

The governing measurement is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. The trace (EV-GPS-00106, weight 1.0) runs 10.78 km against the platform optimal of 7.2 km on EV-TRIP-00106 — an excess of 3.58 km, or 49.72% of the optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established on this trip's own trace. It does NOT reach the materiality gate (over 50% or over 8.0 km), so this is an ordinary, not a material, deviation.

Nothing excuses the route. There is no traffic advisory for the window — the only advisory artifact is missing (EV-ADVIS-00106-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) and its absence is itself citable, but there is nothing for POL-RD-03 to read. The single chat message (EV-CHAT-00106) is the rider asking why the car is at Havelock; it is a question about the route, not an instruction naming a place or road, and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04's test cannot be run and no rider-requested detour is made out. Both endpoints are unamended (POL-RD-05 inapplicable), the vehicle type is RYDE_TAXI not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12 inapplicable), and the fare model is METERED with no quoted fare (POL-RD-11 inapplicable, POL-RD-02 governs).

Refund arithmetic, on separate lines: charged_total 26.04; recomputed_fare 15.32 = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 7.2 km + 0.28 x 19 min) x 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00106, + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP on the optimal route); refund 10.72, rounded UP to 10.75, which is 41.2% of the charge and therefore a partial, not a full, refund. The $5.50 of off-route ERP you objected to is already comprehended inside that figure under POL-RD-09(1) — the recomputed fare contains no gantry because the optimal route crosses none — so it is itemised but must not be added again; the correct figure is 10.75, not 16.25. Both charged gantries are real crossings (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 24.1 m from the gantry coordinates, inside the 250 m radius), so there is no phantom line and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity correction.

No driver pattern is established: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 96 completed trips in 90 days, under both POL-RD-06 tests, so the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b) is unavailable and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No escalation trigger fires: the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 169 fixes, 10 s interval, maximum gap 0.0 s), the trip identifiers all match, no charge line is unmatched, and no exculpatory clause is invoked against an artifact the record lacks. No artifact carrying a deciding fact sits below weight 1.0, so confidence 0.9 stands clear of the 0.70 floor. The driver keeps the rest of the meter and the rider's claim is partially upheld at 10.75.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
